server.name: ny-data-registry-mcp
server.title: New York open data registry MCP server
server.description: An MCP server that finds open data across New York's data portals: which portal covers a place or topic, how to query it, and, from an index BetaNYC builds from the portals' own catalogs, which datasets and columns exist and in what formats. It lists and describes data; it does not serve the data itself.

sources.title: BetaNYC's registry of New York data portals
sources.what: One row per New York data source: the government or organization, its region, its portal and platform, how to reach its API, whether a key is needed, and whether BetaNYC found it live, offline, not yet confirmed, or with no data site.
sources.source_name: New York Data Portal Registry (BetaNYC, grounding-ai-with-ny-open-data)
sources.how_gathered: BetaNYC visits each source's website and records what it finds. A copy ships in the package (data/ny-data-portal-registry.json); when the server starts it checks BetaNYC's published copy for a newer one and keeps it in a cache on your computer. check_source makes one request to a portal's web page when asked and compares the answer with the registry row.

changes.detail: The registry is BetaNYC's own work, checked by hand. This server adds to each row an id, a platform family from a hand-made table (data/platform-families.json), and the place it covers, from a hand-made list of New York's counties, cities, boroughs and regions (data/ny-places.json).

known_gaps: Rows marked not yet confirmed need a person to check them before you rely on them.
The place list (data/ny-places.json) was written by hand and has not been checked against an official gazetteer; a city that spans counties is listed under its main county.

terms.license_name: CC BY-SA 4.0, the license of the repository that publishes the registry
terms.credit_line: Source: BetaNYC, New York Data Portal Registry.

caveats: Endpoints are copied from the registry, never guessed. Rows marked undocumented use an API the owner has not published, which may change.
check_source reports one page request at the moment you ask; a portal that blocks automated requests is reported as blocked, not worked around.

sources.title: Datasets on New York's Socrata portals
sources.what: Titles, descriptions, tags, column names and types, formats, update dates and links for the datasets on New York's Socrata portals, such as NYC Open Data and data.ny.gov.
sources.source_name: Socrata Discovery API (the catalog of each Socrata portal)

publisher.name: New York State, New York City and other New York governments

sources.how_gathered: BetaNYC's harvester reads each portal's catalog through the Socrata Discovery API (Socrata is now the Data and Insights division of Tyler Technologies, per dev.socrata.com), read-only, and builds an index file. The index is published as a GitHub release, and the server downloads it on first run into a cache on your computer. Answers come from that file, with no request to the portals.

changes.detail: Only datasets, maps, files and links are kept. Each dataset is joined to its registry row (place, platform family, portal), and gets download links worked out from Socrata's documented endpoints. find_joinable labels columns as join keys (such as BBL or census tract) from BetaNYC's hand-made table of column names (data/key-columns.json).

known_gaps: Only portals in the registry that run Socrata. Datasets added after the last harvest are missing until the index is rebuilt.

terms.license_name: None stated for the catalog; a dataset's own license, when its portal gives one, is shown with the dataset
terms.credit_line: Dataset descriptions from each portal's own catalog, indexed by BetaNYC.

caveats: This is a catalog of datasets, not the data. Every dataset row links to its page on its own portal: check a dataset's details there.
To report an error in a dataset or its description, use the contact on that dataset's own portal page (Socrata pages have Contact Dataset Owner).
whats_new compares harvests of this index; a dataset is new to the index, which may not be the day the portal published it.
An empty answer means not in this index, not that the data does not exist.

sources.title: Datasets on New York's ArcGIS portals
sources.what: Titles, descriptions, tags, field names and types, formats, update dates and links for the map layers and files on New York's ArcGIS Hub, ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Enterprise portals, mostly county and city sites.
sources.source_name: ArcGIS Hub catalog feeds and ArcGIS portal search (the catalog of each ArcGIS portal)

publisher.name: New York State, New York City and other New York governments

sources.how_gathered: BetaNYC's harvester reads each portal's public catalog (its Hub feed or its portal search, and each layer's field list), read-only and spaced out as each site's robots.txt asks, and builds an index file. The index is published as a GitHub release, and the server downloads it on first run into a cache on your computer. Answers come from that file, with no request to the portals.

changes.detail: Esri's own national layers and items owned by other organizations are left out, as are portals that block automated clients. Each dataset is joined to its registry row (place, platform family, portal). find_joinable labels columns as join keys from BetaNYC's hand-made table of column names (data/key-columns.json).

known_gaps: Only portals in the registry that run ArcGIS and allow automated reading; a portal can be partly harvested when it has more layers than the harvester asks about.
Datasets added after the last harvest are missing until the index is rebuilt.

terms.license_name: None stated for the catalog; each item's own terms of use, when its portal gives them, are shown with the dataset
terms.credit_line: Dataset descriptions from each portal's own catalog, indexed by BetaNYC.

caveats: This is a catalog of datasets, not the data. Every dataset row links to its page on its own portal: check a dataset's details there.
To report an error in a dataset or its description, use the contact on that dataset's own portal page (Socrata pages have Contact Dataset Owner).
ArcGIS Online's terms say public content is typically for personal or noncommercial use, under each item's own terms of use. Check an item's terms before reusing its data.
An empty answer means not in this index, not that the data does not exist.
